title: deskhand shared definitions
description: Shared definitions for the deskhand wire contract (docs/contract.md, 0.9-draft). The $id is an identifier, not a location. Tool schemas reference these with ../defs.json#/$defs/NAME; tools/list serves each tool schema with these definitions copied into its own $defs.
$comment: Every string with a restricted alphabet carries both an anchored pattern and a not-pattern over the forbidden characters. In ECMA-262 the anchored pattern is enough, but in engines where $ also matches before a final line terminator (Python re, and ICU as used by NSRegularExpression) it would accept a trailing newline. The not-pattern closes that gap in every engine.

state.description: deskhand state, listed in precedence order (highest first). 'gated' is amendment 2 and is pending owner approval.

blocking_state.description: Any state other than 'ok', in precedence order.

condition.description: A condition that is reported by status but is not a state. Semantics are in docs/contract.md section 11.

error_code.description: Code carried in structuredContent.code of an isError tool result. JSON-RPC errors use numeric codes instead and never appear here.

holder_id.description: Lease holder label assigned by the caller: 1 to 128 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -. A label, not a credential. Every handle is scoped to (principal, holder_id).

operation_id.description: Caller-supplied idempotency key for one effect call (Crew sends its call ID): 1 to 128 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -. Unique per (principal, holder_id) for the retention window.

frame_id.description: Server-minted opaque handle for one screenshot: 1 to 64 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -. deskhand mints 'frm_' followed by 22 base64url characters; callers treat it as opaque.

sha256.description: Lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest: exactly 64 characters from 0-9 a-f.

timestamp.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp with a literal Z offset and at most 9 fraction digits.

display_id.description: macOS display identifier (CGDirectDisplayID). Valid only within one display_config_generation.

display_config_generation.description: Counter that increases every time the display configuration changes. Strictly increasing within one deskhand process run; compare for equality only.

point.description: A point in global points: origin at the top-left corner of the main display, x to the right, y downward. Coordinates may be negative.

rect.description: A rectangle in global points. The origin may be negative.

frame_coordinate.description: One coordinate in the output pixel space of the named frame. Values that fit this range but fall outside the frame are refused with out_of_frame, not invalid_argument.

frame_point.description: A pixel in the output pixel space of the named frame: (0, 0) is the top-left pixel.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held for the whole action. Pressed in the order control, option, shift, command and released in the reverse order, whatever the array order.

key.description: A key name. A character key names the key that produces that character unshifted in the active keyboard layout.

bundle_id.description: A macOS bundle identifier: 1 to 255 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -. Compared exactly, including case.

permitted_apps.description: Optional caller-side narrowing of the per-Mac app policy. When present, the measured frontmost app, and for pointer calls the app that owns the topmost window under the target (for drag, under the first and the last point of path), must be in this list as well as on the Mac's own allowlist. It can never widen the Mac's policy.

app_ref.description: An application as measured by deskhand.

bundle_id.description: Null when the process has no bundle identifier.

team_id.description: Code-signing team identifier, or null when unsigned or unavailable.

measured.description: Facts deskhand measured at the app-policy check immediately before the first event of an effect call. On a denied_app that aborts a call part-way, the facts measured at the check that failed.

target_app.description: pointer: the app that owns the topmost window under the first target point. keyboard: null.

window_title.description: pointer: title of the topmost window under the first target point. keyboard: title of the frontmost app's focused window. Null when there is no window or the title is unavailable. Truncated to 512 characters.

global_point.description: pointer: the global point the first target mapped to. keyboard: null.

operation_status.description: Lifecycle state of an operation record. accepted and executing are transient; the rest are terminal.

operation_view.description: The operation record as it stood when the response was produced.

events_posted.description: Input events posted for this operation, excluding release events posted by cleanup. A lower bound when status is aborted_by_restart.

stale_frame_reason.description: Why a frame was refused, in the order the checks run. Diagnostic only: the remedy is always a new screenshot.

lease_view.description: The live lease as visible to the caller.

holder_id.description: The holder label. Null when the lease is held under a different principal.

expires_in_ms.description: Milliseconds until expires_at by deskhand's clock. Callers schedule renewal from this value, not from expires_at, so clock skew does not matter.

effect_result.description: structuredContent of a successful pointer or keyboard call.

replayed.description: True when this is the stored result of an earlier call with the same operation_id. Nothing was posted by this call.

tool_error.description: structuredContent of every isError tool result.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Not stable; never parse it.

state.description: The highest-precedence state at the moment the error was produced.

operation.description: The record for this operation_id, whichever call created it. Present exactly when such a record exists. Absent means no input was ever posted for this operation_id.

replayed.description: Present exactly when this is the result of an admitted call: false when first returned, true when it is the stored result returned to a repeat.

retry_after_ms.description: Earliest useful retry, in milliseconds. Required for rate_limited.

details.description: Code-specific detail. Keys are listed per code in docs/contract.md section 9.2.

argument.description: JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into arguments naming the offending value.
